figures.caption: Figure 4: Identified set of the net social surplus in a stylized example from Kang and Vasserman (2025). The area between the dotted red lines is where the decision problem is nontrivial and where the global least favorable point is located.

Figure 1: Two different asymptotics in the stylized example. Left: we localize at any µ0. As a result, I (µ0 + h/ √ n) → I(µ0) as n → ∞. Right: we localize at µ0 = 0 and consider a local parameter space Θn implying a shrinking identified set.

Figure 5: Left: Illustration of Mµ,∞ in the evidence aggregation example when C1 = C2 = C. The highlighted area represents {µ ∈ Mµ,∞ : I (1) (0;µ) ≥ 0}. Nature’s equilibrium choice of (µ1, µ2) in the limit game is along the red line whenever ρ ≤ min{σ1/σ2, σ2/σ1}. Right: A 3D illustration of the parameter space in the same example.

Figure 2: A global least favorable point in the example of Section 2.1. On µ-axis, every point to the left of the orange dot and to the right of the blue dot leads to R(µ) = 0. Between these two points, R(µ) is strictly positive and maximized at the red dot with a value of k/2.
Figure 3: Parameter space in limit game (21) (from left to right: κ0 < 1, κ0 = 1 and κ0 > 1)
